title: Natufian culture, Levant: settled foragers before farming
summary: The Natufians were late Epipaleolithic foragers of the Levant, about 15,000–11,500 years ago, whose growing sedentism accompanied a shift from foraging toward farming. Mount Carmel's caves hold Natufian burials and early stone architecture, a 12,000-year-old grave at Hilazon Tachtit is a rare window on their beliefs, and Natufians at Shubayqa 1 in Jordan baked bread from wild cereals over 14,000 years ago.

uncertainty.note: Range 15,000–11,500 cal BP as given by UNESCO and a PNAS paper; BP is converted at 1950.
